review.requirement_proposition: AI systems should remain robust, secure and safe throughout their entire lifecycle, functioning appropriately without unreasonable safety or security risks under normal use, foreseeable use or misuse and other adverse conditions.
review.reason_for_change: The reported outage is established, but Kiro’s role in producing the engineering change is disputed. The causal trace linking the AI workflow to the service consequence is decisive and unavailable.

review.requirement_proposition: Enable investigators to trace the system processes that led to an incident over the relevant time period.

conclusion_change.previous: A bounded AWS service outage occurred, but the available public accounts conflict about whether Kiro had a causal role. VIGIL therefore assesses the materialised service consequence separately from the disputed mechanism and retains an ambiguous mechanism-attribution relationship. The service consequence and disputed Kiro mechanism remain separate. The retained ambiguous mechanism-attribution relationship is a substantive boundary result, not a concluded AI-causation failure or proof that subsequent peer review prevented every recurrence.
conclusion_change.new: The service outage is established while AI causation remains disputed. Security and investigator-traceability assessments remain unresolved pending an occurrence-specific process trace. The finding does not assign the outage to Kiro or infer that later peer review prevents every recurrence.
